Burnet County Commissioners Court’s                                                 2
Exceptions to Proposal for Decision
 TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSIONERS:

         Burnet County Commissioners Court (“BCCC”) timely files its Exceptions to the

Proposal for Decision.

         BCCC wishes to thank the Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) for giving time

back to the Intervenors before the hearing. Even the additional four days provided the

Intervenors and their counsel with valuable time to prepare for the hearing. Joint

Applicants’ requirement of ten business-days (two weeks) to respond to discovery requests

caused Joint Applicants’ discovery answers to be due after the hearing began.

         BCCC also thanks the ALJs for their thoughtful analysis of the issues presented in

this case. Finally, BCCC appreciates the ALJs’ consideration of BCCC’s arguments

concerning proposed ordering paragraphs that would require the Joint Applicants to

conduct a study regarding potential interference with BCCC’s emergency management

communication equipment.

         BCCC respectfully asks the Commission to reevaluate its request to add ordering

paragraphs protecting BCCC’s emergency management communication equipment and

modify the PFD accordingly. BCCC submits the following Exceptions to the Proposal for

Decision (“PFD”).

    I.       SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT

         BCCC agrees with the PFD that Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC. (“Oncor”)

and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation (“LCRA”) (together “Joint Applicants)

failed to meet their burdens in their Joint Application and that the Joint Application should

be denied.

         BCCC also agrees with the PFD that Joint Applicants failed to provide landowners

with proper notice under the Commission’s rules. In addition, the PFD and Joint Applicants

Burnet County Commissioners Court’s          3
Exceptions to Proposal for Decision
 failed to include necessary protections against interference by transmission towers and

lines with Burnet County’s emergency management communication systems and its

connection to the Statewide Interoperability Communication System.

           Finally, Joint Applicants did not carry their burden to show need for these massive

745kV transmission lines at this time.

    II.          NOTICE

           BCCC agrees with the PFD that Joint Applicants did not provide notice of the Joint

Application in accordance with 16 TAC §22.52 (3) and (4) for the facts, reasons and

conclusions as set forth in the PFD.1


    III.         CONSTRAINTS

           Joint Applicants’ witness Russell Marusak admitted that Joint Applicants were not

aware of the locations of the BCCC Emergency Management Communications towers.2

Joint Applicants’ witness admitted that he had neither experience nor knowledge of Fresnel

Zone Encroachment with emergency public safety communication infrastructure.3 The

main witness testifying on the issue, Mr. Dave Elliot, testified that he reviewed an EPRI

article the Saturday night before the hearing.4 Mr. Elliott could only answer questions

relating to interference between the general frequency of the transmission lines to what his

assumed frequency for the emergency communications infrastructure. 5              Mr. Elliott

admitted that independent of the operating voltage interference, interference with radio


           1
               PFD at pp. 26-36 (Aug. 20, 2026).
           2 Tr. Vol. 2 at p. 28:8-25.

           3
               Tr. Vol. 2 at p. 32:6-14.
           4
               Id. at pp. 29:22; 30:9-12; p. 32:1-3.
           5 Id. at pp. 29:1-33:21.




Burnet County Commissioners Court’s                    4
Exceptions to Proposal for Decision
 communications could occur driven by “gap discharge” and “corona discharge.”6 Mr.

Elliott testified that the Joint Applicants “were testing for that.” 7 Finally, Mr. Elliot

admitted that Joint Applicants have not done any studies regarding these issues.8

        Obviously, because Joint Applicants do not know what Fresnel Zone Encroachment

is, they have no idea whether the placement of the transmission lines or towers will interfere

with the emergency management safety communication towers installed in Burnet County.

And they currently do not know where the BCCC emergency management

communications are located.

        The PFD noted that Joint Applicants’ (Ms. Cooley’s) testimony at the hearing that

Oncor would work with BCCC to mitigate any issues that may arise9 and then declined to

added BCCC’s requested ordering paragraphs. If Joint Applicants actually had any

experience or knowledge with this issue, perhaps such a representation at the hearing is

sufficient. But the evidence shows that Joint Applicants have NO knowledge with how the

transmission equipment could affect emergency public safety communications as to

Fresnel Zone Encroachment and are just starting to test for how gap discharge and corona

discharge can affect it.10 Joint Applicants then argue in their Reply Brief that it was the

burden of BCCC to prove with expert testimony that interference could take place.11 But

constraints are the burden of the Joint Applicants to avoid, not the County’s to prove.




        6
            Id. at p. 30:13-22.
        7
            Id. at p. 30:17-18.
        8
            Id. at p. 31:7-18.
        9 Id. at pp. 33:22-34.6.

        10 Tr. Vol. 2 at pp. 31:19-32:5.

        11 Applicants’ Reply Brief at pp. 58-59.




Burnet County Commissioners Court’s                5
Exceptions to Proposal for Decision
           PUC Staff witness, John Poole, agreed that preventing interference with BCCC’s

emergency public safety communication systems was sufficiently important for the

Commission to include in the order.12

          Because Joint Applicants agreed that they would mitigate any interference, they

should have no problem with adding ordering paragraphs that achieve this purpose rather

than relying on the standard ordering language.              The emergency public safety

communication equipment is new to Burnet County, which is a rural area. This will not be

a one-time issue.

    IV.       NEED

          The PFD analyzed the record evidence in this docket, thoroughly evaluated and

eloquently described why the Joint Applicants did not carry their burden of proving need

in this docket.13 The Burnet County Commissioners Court agrees the PFD.

    V.        CONCLUSION

          BCCC respectfully requests the Commission deny the Joint Application because:

          a. the information in the environmental assessment in inaccurate and stale because

              Joint Applicants did not follow the Commission rule 16 TAC 22.52 (3) and (4);

          b. legislation did not order that the solutions to the Permian Basin need be limited

              to transmission-only; and

          c. the information in the ERCOT PBRS is limited to transmission-only.

          In the alternative, BCCC requests that the decision in this docket be delayed until

the additional deficiencies as stated above are corrected.




          12 Tr. Vol. 2. at p. 147:18-23.

          13 PFD at pp. 52-99.



Burnet County Commissioners Court’s            6
Exceptions to Proposal for Decision
         If the Commission finds that the Joint Applicants carried their burden in this

proceeding, BCCC requests that ordering paragraphs be included as follows:

        1. Before completing engineering and design of any transmission towers or lines,

            Joint Applicants shall commission a study on the potential interference of

            765kV transmission lines and towers with Burnet County Commissioners

            Court’s emergency public safety communications systems, including potential

            Fresnel Zone Encroachment, gap discharge interference and corona discharge

            interference.

        2. Joint Applicants shall survey the location of Burnet County emergency

            communication towers in Burnet County to determine the actual locations of

            the emergency public safety communication towers.

        3. Joint Applicants shall consult with Burnet County Commissioners Court to

            mitigate any potential interference with Burnet County’s emergency public

            safety communications systems.




                              CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
        I certify that a copy of this document was served on all parties of record on
September 2, 2026, in accordance with P.U.C. Procedural Rule 22.74 and Orders issued to
date in Docket 59475.

                                                   Margaret Uhlig Pemberton
